text:
Recent work supports extracting structured attributes from available titles/descriptions while preserving missingness. [WDC-PAVE (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02130) evaluates extraction plus normalization, including unit conversion and name normalization, against manually verified annotations. [ExtractGPT](https://github.com/wbsg-uni-mannheim/ExtractGPT) explicitly specifies “n/a” for absent attributes. Applied here: extract artist, media format, device/model compatibility and specifications only with supporting text spans; distinguish an explicit compatibility claim, an explicit conflict and unknown information. Shared brand or broad topic alone cannot establish usability. The [2024 knowledge-based recommendation overview](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/big-data/articles/10.3389/fdata.2024.1304439/full) supports reasoning about explicit requirements and conflicts.

Grounded explanations also need preference relevance: [PURE (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03080) identifies factually correct but preference-inconsistent explanations and selects evidence for specificity and alignment. [Attribute or Abstain (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07799) studies evidence attribution and abstention, although outside recommendation. Suggested probes: supported-attribute coverage, explicit-conflict rate among assessable pairs, unknown rate, repeated artist/format concentration and near-duplicate title frequency. Treat repetition as descriptive redundancy, not evidence of dissatisfaction or unobserved diversity preferences.

Before interpreting these probes, audit a small sample stratified across all four datasets, including missing and conflicting descriptions. Manually label extraction spans, normalized values and feedback codes; report extraction precision/recall, coding agreement and denominators. Vary confidence thresholds to examine error versus coverage. Keep unsupported feedback unclassified; interaction history establishes neither ownership nor satisfaction. These are proposed diagnostics, not measured findings or substitutes for the fixed macro validation HR@10.
